metadata.topic: Transport — Substances Found in Blood (other than cells and platelets)
metadata.note: 3m: name THREE other substances found in blood. 5 correct options for 3 slots — any 3 of 5 earn full marks. Follows Q5a(i) where students identified RBC/WBC/Platelet functions. 'Other substances' means dissolved/transported substances in plasma, not the cellular components.

question.name: CSEC Bio May 2022 Q5a(ii) — Name Three Other Substances Found in Blood
question.text:
Name THREE other substances which are found in the blood:

Substance 1: [[1]]

Substance 2: [[2]]

Substance 3: [[3]]
question.general_feedback:
Other substances found in blood (in addition to blood cells and platelets):

  • Plasma — the liquid part of blood (mainly water) that carries all other substances
  • Glucose — dissolved sugar transported from the digestive system to body cells for respiration
  • Hormones — chemical messengers (e.g. insulin, adrenaline) transported from glands to target organs
  • Urea — metabolic waste product from protein breakdown, transported to the kidneys for excretion
  • Antibodies — proteins produced by white blood cells to combat pathogens

Also acceptable: Oxygen (dissolved/carried by haemoglobin), Carbon dioxide, Mineral salts, Amino acids, Fatty acids, Vitamins, Fibrinogen (clotting protein)

groups.label: First substance transported in blood (other than cells)
groups.diagnostic_hint: Many substances are transported dissolved in blood plasma. Common examples include glucose (energy), hormones (chemical messengers), urea (waste), and antibodies (immune proteins).

groups.label: Second substance transported in blood (other than cells)
groups.diagnostic_hint: Select a substance different from your first answer. Red blood cells and haemoglobin are disqualifiers — the question asks for substances OTHER than named blood cells.

groups.label: Third substance transported in blood (other than cells)
groups.diagnostic_hint: A third distinct substance. Note: haemoglobin is found INSIDE red blood cells, not dissolved freely in plasma — it does not count as a dissolved blood substance.

ddwtos.word_bank_note: 7 tokens for 3 slots. 5 correct substances — any 3 of 5 earn full marks (engine awards mark for any correct token in each slot; student must not repeat the same token). 'Red blood cells' is the trap distractor: the question specifies 'other substances' meaning substances OTHER THAN blood cells/platelets (which were named in Q5a(i)). 'Haemoglobin (in cells only)' is a subtle distractor — haemoglobin is found inside RBCs, not freely dissolved in plasma in a healthy person; CSEC mark schemes do not accept this as a blood substance in the plasma sense. Plasma is itself a correct answer (it IS a substance found in blood, distinct from cells). All 5 correct tokens represent common, expected CSEC answers: plasma/glucose/hormones/urea/antibodies.
